record.paper_title: Open Problems in the Function Theory of the Bergman Space
record.context_brief: Adding a zero to a Bergman zero divisor
record.original_question: For every zero sequence A of L2_a(D), does the quotient G_{A union {0}} / G_A belong to the Smirnov space on D, where the Smirnov space consists of quotients f/g with f and g bounded analytic functions on D and g outer?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2. Does G_{A∪{0}}/G_A always belong to the Smirnov space on D? The Smirnov space consists of all quotients f/g, where f, g ∈ H∞(D), and g is an outer function.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{D}=\{z\in\mathbb{C}:|z|<1\}$ denote the open unit disk, and let $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ be the (unweighted) Bergman space of analytic functions $f$ on $\mathbb{D}$ for which $\|f\|^2=\int_{\mathbb{D}}|f(z)|^2\,dA(z)<\infty$, where $dA$ is normalized area measure. A sequence $A=\{a_j\}\subset\mathbb{D}$ (with multiplicities) is called a zero sequence for $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ if there exists a non-trivial function in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ whose zero set, counted with multiplicities, equals $A$. For such a zero sequence $A$, let $I_A$ denote the closed subspace of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ consisting of all functions vanishing on $A$ (with multiplicities), and let $G_A$ denote the canonical (contractive) zero divisor associated with $A$, i.e. the unique extremal solution to the problem
$$\sup\{\mathrm{Re}\,f(0)/z_A : f\in I_A,\ \|f\|=1\},$$
suitably normalized, so that $G_A$ is the canonical Bergman zero divisor.

Define the Smirnov space on $\mathbb{D}$ to be
$$N^+(\mathbb{D}) = \{f/g : f,g\in H^\infty(\mathbb{D}),\ g\text{ is outer}\},$$
where $H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ is the algebra of bounded analytic functions on $\mathbb{D}$ and a function $g\in H^\infty(\mathbb{D})$ is outer if $\log|g(0)|=\int_0^{2\pi}\log|g(e^{i\theta})|\,\frac{d\theta}{2\pi}$.

Question: For every zero sequence $A$ of $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ (with $0\notin A$), does the quotient $G_{A\cup\{0\}}/G_A$ belong to the Smirnov space $N^+(\mathbb{D})$?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not reveal a published resolution of this specific question concerning whether quotients of canonical Bergman zero divisors $G_{A\cup\{0\}}/G_A$ always lie in the Smirnov class. Closely related works by Hedenmalm, Aleman, Duren–Khavinson–Shapiro–Sundberg study contractive divisors and their multiplier/expansive properties, but none located here state a definitive answer to this particular quotient-membership question. Current status could not be confirmed from the available sources.

status_evidence.title: Curious properties of canonical divisors in weighted Bergman spaces (Aleman–Hedenmalm)
status_evidence.snippet: Study of properties of canonical (contractive) zero divisors in (weighted) Bergman spaces; addresses subtle multiplier and factorization properties but does not appear to settle the Smirnov-class membership of $G_{A\cup\{0\}}/G_A$.
status_evidence.claim: Related investigations into canonical Bergman divisors exist but no resolution of the specific Smirnov-quotient problem is confirmed.

status_evidence.title: Beurling's Theorem for the Bergman space (Aleman–Richter–Sundberg)
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes Beurling-type theorems for invariant subspaces in the Bergman space; central reference for divisor theory in $L^2_a(\mathbb{D})$ but does not state the Smirnov-class quotient property in question.
status_evidence.claim: Major structural results on Bergman invariant subspaces do not address this specific quotient question.
